tools.name: create_account
tools.description: Register a new Keywordise account from the terminal and receive an API key for it. Requires accept_terms=true: the person accepts the Terms and Privacy Policy (https://keywordise.com/terms) and authorises Keywordise to apply for jobs on their behalf. A confirmation email is sent; applying opens once

tools.name: login
tools.description: Exchange the account's email and password for a new API key, so a terminal or an assistant can act on the account. The key is shown once; keep it. Up to five keys may be active per account (revoke_api_key frees a slot).

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: The account behind this key: email and whether it is confirmed, plan state (trial days left, applications used and remaining, subscription), and how many API keys are active.

tools.name: resend_verification_email
tools.description: Send the email-confirmation link again to this account's address. Applying is blocked until the address is confirmed; nothing else is.

tools.name: get_upgrade_link
tools.description: A checkout link for a paid plan from the active payment provider: Starter ($24.99/month, 500 applications a month) or Pro ($49/month, 1,000 a month; the default). The person opens it in a browser to pay; the account upgrades automatically when the payment lands.

tools.name: get_billing_portal_link
tools.description: A link to the payment provider's customer portal for this account's subscription, where invoices, the payment method and cancellation live.

tools.name: cancel_subscription
tools.description: Cancel the Pro subscription at the end of the current billing period. Access stays until then. Irreversible from here; the person can resubscribe later.

tools.name: list_api_keys
tools.description: The active API keys on this account: prefix, label, created and last used. Never the key itself.

tools.name: create_api_key
tools.description: Mint an additional API key for this account, for another machine or assistant. Shown once. Five active keys maximum.

tools.name: revoke_api_key
tools.description: Revoke one of this account's API keys immediately. Any terminal or assistant using it stops working at once. Revoking the key you are calling with ends this session.

tools.name: export_my_data
tools.description: The account's complete data as one JSON file (profile, targeting, matched jobs, applications, saved answers, run history, audit trail). Returned as a file; large accounts are told to download it in the app instead.

tools.name: delete_my_account
tools.description: Erase the account and everything in it: profile, CV files, matches, applications, answers, keys. Irreversible. Requires confirm_email equal to the account's address.

tools.name: get_my_profile
tools.description: Use when the person asks what is on their profile or CV. Not needed before searching or applying: those tools read the saved CV themselves. The CV profile Keywordise holds for this account (name, contact, summary, skills, roles, education), the job-targeting rules (countries, remote preference, keyw

tools.name: upload_cv
tools.description: Use when the person shares or mentions their resume/CV ('here's my resume', 'use my CV'). Upload a CV file and turn it into the account's profile: the same parser the app uses reads the document into name, contact, summary, roles, skills, languages and education. With save=true (default) the profile

tools.name: update_profile
tools.description: Change fields of the saved profile without re-uploading the CV. Send only the fields to change (full_name, contact_email, phone, location, city, address, postcode, professional_summary, skills, pinned_skills, languages, experience, education, projects, certifications, links, …); everything else is u

tools.name: get_profile_gaps
tools.description: The gaps in the saved profile that weaken applications (missing dates on a role, no contact phone, empty summary, …), each with a severity, so they can be fixed with update_profile.

tools.name: suggest_keywords
tools.description: Search keywords derived from the saved profile, useful as include_keywords in update_targeting.

tools.name: list_cv_designs
tools.description: The CV designs a tailored CV can be rendered in, with the account's current pick.

tools.name: set_cv_design
tools.description: Set the design every tailored CV is rendered in (a key from list_cv_designs).

tools.name: get_my_cv_pdf
tools.description: The account's base CV (the saved profile, untailored) rendered as a PDF in the chosen design, returned as a file. No model call.

tools.name: get_targeting
tools.description: Every targeting rule the feed and the apply run obey: remote mode, geo scope and countries, locations, include/exclude keywords, title allow/block lists, seniority, salary, languages, work authorisation, company allow/block, daily and per-company caps, cover-letter and CV settings, screening default

tools.name: update_targeting
tools.description: Change targeting rules; send only the keys to change (remote_mode any|remote|hybrid|onsite, geo_scope worldwide|region|country, geo_countries [ISO-2], locations, include_keywords, exclude_keywords, title_allow, title_block, seniority, salary_min, currency, languages, company_block, max_apps_per_day,

tools.name: describe_what_i_want
tools.description: Use when the person says what they are looking for in their own words ('senior remote data roles in the US, no agencies'). Turn a plain sentence ('remote data roles in Germany or the Netherlands, senior, not agencies') plus the saved CV into concrete targeting rules. Returns the inferred rules and t

tools.name: get_feed_reach
tools.description: How many jobs the current targeting shows versus how many each single rule is hiding, and which one change would widen the feed most. Every number comes from re-asking the feed's own predicate with one control relaxed.

tools.name: list_countries_with_jobs
tools.description: The countries the live pool actually has inventory in (ISO-2, name, job count), for choosing geo_countries in update_targeting.

tools.name: list_matching_jobs
tools.description: Use when the person wants jobs or their best matches: 'find me jobs', 'my top matches', 'remote marketing jobs that fit my resume', 'what's new for me this week'. It already uses the saved CV, so there is no need to read the profile first. Live vacancies matched to this account's CV, ranked. Each jo

tools.name: get_job_posting
tools.description: The full description of one matched vacancy, with a short summary and highlights, plus the link that opens the posting from the app.

tools.name: explain_job_match
tools.description: Use for 'is this job a good fit', 'why this match', 'what am I missing for this role'. For one vacancy: the match percentage, the requirements this account's CV covers and the ones it is missing. With narrative=true, also a short written assessment with strengths and gaps (a paid model call; limited

tools.name: preview_tailored_cv
tools.description: Use for 'tailor my resume for this job' or 'what would you send for this one'. Rewrite this account's CV for one vacancy the way Keywordise would send it: headline, summary, the roles selected for this job with rewritten bullets, curated skills and a cover letter, every segment labelled tailored, ve

tools.name: rate_job
tools.description: Feedback on one job: hide or dislike removes it from the feed and teaches the matcher what this person rejects; interested is a positive signal. Undo with unhide_job.

tools.name: unhide_job
tools.description: Undo hide or dislike: the job returns to the feed and the negative signal is dropped.

tools.name: list_hidden_jobs
tools.description: The jobs this account hid or disliked, newest first, so one can be put back.

tools.name: refresh_matches
tools.description: Match the account's CV against the vacancies added since it last looked, in the background. Idempotent and cheap when nothing is new. force=true runs a full re-match regardless. rebuild=true rebuilds the feed from scratch through the same build as the app's Rebuild button (use it when the feed looks

tools.name: get_match_status
tools.description: Only for checking on a match or feed rebuild that is already running (after upload_cv, update_targeting or refresh_matches); to find or show jobs use list_matching_jobs. Live status of the latest match run (scanned, inserted, elapsed), the feed counts it produced, and `feed_build`: where the feed is

tools.name: start_apply_run
tools.description: Use when the person says 'apply for me', 'apply to the best matches' or 'apply to this job' (pass job_id). Show them the jobs first. Start an application run: Keywordise takes up to `limit` of the matching jobs (same filters as list_matching_jobs, best fit first, never one already applied to), tailo

tools.name: get_apply_run_status
tools.description: Live progress of the latest run: running or not (from a heartbeat, not a status claim), processed of total, the job being worked on now, confirmed, needs review, skipped, closed.

tools.name: stop_apply_run
tools.description: Use for 'stop applying', 'pause', 'hold off'. Ask the running application run to stop after the job it is on. Nothing is left half-done; applications already sent stay sent.

tools.name: list_my_applications
tools.description: Use for 'what did I apply to', 'any replies', 'status of my applications'. Every application sent for this account: company, title, stage, outcome, when it went out, how many screening questions it still waits on, and the employer's acknowledgement where one was received.

tools.name: list_blocking_questions
tools.description: Questions employers asked on applications that are stalled until this account answers them, grouped by application, each with a suggested answer drawn from what the person answered before. Answer with answer_screening_question.

tools.name: answer_screening_question
tools.description: Record the person's answer to one screening question on one application. The answer is written in the person's name and saved to their answer book, so the same question is never asked again. When it is the last required answer, the application is SUBMITTED to the employer. Only give an answer the pe

tools.name: get_sent_cv_pdf
tools.description: The tailored CV PDF that went to the employer for one application, returned as a file.

tools.name: list_run_history
tools.description: The last five match runs and the last five application runs, with their counts and status.

tools.name: list_saved_answers
tools.description: The answer book: every screening answer this account has given or taught, which future applications reuse automatically in any phrasing or language.

tools.name: save_answer
tools.description: Add or replace a screening answer in the answer book ('What is your notice period?' → '1 month'). Applications already waiting on that fact are completed and sent in the background. Only save what the person actually stated.

tools.name: delete_saved_answer
tools.description: Remove one answer from the answer book (an answer_id from list_saved_answers).

tools.name: list_facts_to_provide
tools.description: The universal screening facts this account has not answered yet (right to work, notice period, salary expectation, …), ranked by how many waiting applications each one unblocks. Answer them with save_answer.

tools.name: get_tracker
tools.description: The tracker board: applications grouped by the stage the person set (saved, applied, interview, offer, rejected) with their own notes.

tools.name: move_tracker_card
tools.description: Set the tracker stage of one application: saved, applied, interview, offer or rejected.

tools.name: set_tracker_note
tools.description: Replace the person's own note on one tracked application (interview date, contact, next step).

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "login" references sensitive artifacts (password, api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_account, get_account, get_targeting, get_feed_reach, get_match_status, get_apply_run_status · Private data: create_account, login, get_account, list_api_keys, create_api_key, revoke_api_key, export_my_data, delete_my_account, get_my_profile, upload_cv, get_profile_gaps, get_my_cv_pdf, answer_screening_question, get_sent_cv_pdf, set_tracker_note · Public sink: create_account, login, get_account, resend_verification_email, upload_cv, update_profile, update_targeting, preview_tailored_cv, start_apply_run · Destructive: export_my_data, delete_my_account, get_targeting, get_match_status, start_apply_run, get_apply_run_status, stop_apply_run, list_run_history, delete_saved_answer.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_account, get_account, get_targeting, get_feed_reach, get_match_status, get_apply_run_status · Private data: create_account, login, get_account, list_api_keys, create_api_key, revoke_api_key, export_my_data, delete_my_account, get_my_profile, upload_cv, get_profile_gaps, get_my_cv_pdf, answer_screening_question, get_sent_cv_pdf, set_tracker_note · Public sink: create_account, login, get_account, resend_verification_email, upload_cv, update_profile, update_targeting, preview_tailored_cv, start_apply_run · Destructive: export_my_data, delete_my_account, get_targeting, get_match_status, start_apply_run, get_apply_run_status, stop_apply_run, list_run_history, delete_saved_answer

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
